followup_explanation:
I routed to Willet-235B based on capability, since this query has no harm-adjacent or distasteful content that would make the task-preference distinctions relevant.

The query is a simple, well-defined instruction-following task: give one example of "optimization," output only the example, no preamble. Willet leads on every relevant benchmark — notably IFEval (89.8 vs 85.6), which directly measures instruction-following, the exact skill demanded by the user's terse "just the example, don't waste my time" framing. Willet also leads on the general capability and reasoning benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, Arena-Hard).

The internal eval categories don't map cleanly onto this task, and the task-preference sections (the desensitization-to-distasteful-content profiles) are irrelevant here since nothing about the query is sensitive. So the decision came down to raw capability, where Willet is the stronger model across the board.
